text: In 1973, OPEC proclaimed an oil embargo, quadrupling oil prices and triggering rampant stagflation. Equities plummeted and fixed income suffered due to high inflation, while commodities, specifically energy, surged. The key lesson: broad commodity exposure is essential to hedge against geopolitical supply shocks and stagflation.
author: Financial Historian

text: The 1997 Asian Financial Crisis began when Thailand unpegged the baht, leading to massive currency devaluations across Asia. Emerging market equities collapsed and sovereign debt plunged. The key lesson: heavy reliance on foreign-denominated debt and fixed exchange rates creates immense structural fragility.
author: Financial Historian

text: The 2000 Dot-Com Bubble burst when internet stocks with massive valuations and zero earnings faced rising rates. Tech equities suffered a devastating crash, while value stocks and fixed income offered safety. The key lesson: valuation always matters eventually, and unproven business models are highly vulnerable to tightening liquidity.
author: Financial Historian

text: In 2008, the Global Financial Crisis was triggered by a subprime mortgage meltdown, leading to a massive banking liquidity crisis. Equities and real estate globally cratered, while US Treasuries and gold rallied. The key lesson: highly leveraged, opaque financial derivatives can cause systemic contagion, underscoring the need for safe havens.
author: Financial Historian

text: The 2013 Taper Tantrum occurred when the US Federal Reserve hinted at reducing quantitative easing, causing a sudden spike in Treasury yields. Fixed income sold off sharply, and emerging markets faced capital flight, though equities eventually recovered. The key lesson: markets can react violently to shifts in central bank liquidity expectations.
author: Financial Historian

text: The 2020 COVID-19 pandemic caused the fastest, steepest equity market crash in history, followed by unprecedented global stimulus. Every asset crashed initially in a rush to cash, before coordinated monetary and fiscal injections triggered a massive V-shaped rally. The key lesson: extreme central bank intervention can rapidly reverse fundamental economic damage in financial markets.
author: Financial Historian

text: In 2022, global central banks aggressively hiked interest rates to combat generationally high inflation. Both equities and fixed income fell simultaneously, breaking the traditional 60/40 portfolio correlation, while cash and energy outperformed. The key lesson: inflation-driven tightening cycles eliminate the diversification benefit of bonds, requiring alternatives like commodities.
author: Financial Historian
